subject: Re: Red team report — methodology, firm credentials, and report-age acceptance
messages:
From: Elena Morales <sec@acme.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question: Red team report and acceptance window

Hi Connor / Marissa,

We're preparing the SOC 2 evidence package for Acme's upcoming audit and want to confirm whether the red team report you previously provided will satisfy the auditor. Details: the report is from RedSky Security (report date: 2025-10-12).

Two quick questions:
- Is a report that is ~10 months old acceptable under Redwood's policy for a SOC 2 attestation?
- Can you provide a short explanation of RedSky's methodology and their firm credentials (accreditations, sample test types) so we can map to our auditor's expectations?

Auditor asked for confirmation that: external attack surface, credentialed testing where relevant, vulnerability verification (exploitation or proof-of-concept), and remediation verification are covered. If remediation verification is not in the report, will Redwood accept vendor attestation plus a remediation workbook, or do auditors typically insist on a retest?

If you can share a short guidance note (1 page) we can include in the evidence pack. Also please flag any items you think the auditor will push back on.

Thanks — tight timeline on our side; audit window opens 2026-09-15.

Best,
Elena Morales
Security Program Manager
Acme Corp
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <sec@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question: Red team report and acceptance window

Elena — thanks for the note and the timeline. Quick summary up front: the RedSky report from 2025-10-12 is likely acceptable as SOC 2 evidence if a couple of conditions are met; otherwise a short retest or an attestation + remediation verification will be needed.

High-level Redwood position (to help your auditor):
- Report age: we accept third-party test reports up to 12 months old from the report date for SOC 2 evidence. Given the 2025-10-12 date, the report is ~10 months old today and falls within our acceptance window.
- Firm credentials: we require independent vendors with established penetration testing practices. Common signals we check: references, published methodology, evidence of industry-recognized training/assessments for testers, and insurance/engagement contracts. CREST/OSCP/etc. are helpful signals but not strict requirements; we validate by reviewing the vendor's credentials and sample engagement notes.
- Methodology coverage: auditors typically want confirmation of: external surface enumeration, authenticated (credentialed) testing where applicable, exploitation/proof-of-concept for high/critical findings, and either remediation verification or a remediation plan plus attestation that fixes were applied.

Options for you (pick one):
1) Use the existing RedSky report + a remediation workbook (spreadsheet) that shows remediation items, owners, and closure dates, plus a short RedSky attestation that they reviewed fixes (no retest). This is usually sufficient for SOC 2 if the attestation explicitly states remediation verification.
2) If the auditor insists on technical verification, schedule a scoped retest/validation with RedSky (they can provide a limited-scope recheck for closed items).

Requested artifacts I can help assemble:
- One-page guidance note summarizing RedSky methodology vs auditor requirements (I'll prepare).
- A concise attestation template for RedSky to sign.
- A remediation workbook template (we recommend the format) you can populate.

Hannah — tagging you for visibility (audit help / evidence checklist). Marissa — can you confirm we have the RedSky credentials PDF and whether remediation verification was performed at the time of the original engagement?

Connor O'Brien
Senior Security Partner, Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132
From: Diego Rios <reports@redskysec.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Morales <sec@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Red team report — methodology & credentials (RedSky)

Connor / Elena — thanks for the ping. RedSky confirms the following against your questions: 

Engagement summary:
- Report date: 2025-10-12 (external red team + web app credentialed testing).
- Scope: external perimeter, public APIs, customer-facing web application, and a limited credentialed internal network test (as agreed in SOW).

Methodology & standards:
- We follow NIST SP 800-115 techniques for test design, OWASP ASVS where relevant for web controls, and perform proof-of-concept exploits for high/critical findings.
- Testers on this engagement: 3 senior testers (lead holds OSCP + CRT), and one specialist for web exploitation.
- Deliverables include: executive summary, technical findings with PoCs, risk ratings, and recommendations. The original engagement did not include a full retest; we did provide verification steps and reproduction instructions for remediation.

Firm credentials:
- RedSky Security LLC — team certifications include OSCP, CREST training, and several testers with prior corporate red team experience. We can provide a short vendor cred pack (pdf).

Remediation verification options:
- We can provide a signed attestation confirming RedSky reviewed remediation artifacts and determined fixes were reasonable based on evidence provided by the customer (screenshot/patch details).
- Alternatively, we can run a focused retest of closed items (2–4 business days) for a small fee or apply a retest credit if agreed in the original contract.

Attachments: redsky_credentials.pdf (1-page vendor cred pack).

If you want, we can sign the attestation template Connor mentioned and/or schedule a retest for early September.

— Diego
Director of Assessments, RedSky Security
reports@redskysec.com

Summary:
- The RedSky 2025-10-12 report is within our 12-month acceptance window and is provisionally acceptable for SOC 2 evidence.
- To close the loop for auditors we need either: (A) a RedSky attestation confirming remediation verification for critical/high items plus a populated remediation workbook, or (B) a focused retest for verified closures.

Actions I have taken / attachments:

- Attached: redsky_credentials.pdf (from RedSky).

Requested from Acme:

- If you want RedSky to provide the attestation, reply-all and Diego will confirm acceptance and sign. If you prefer a retest, tell us which findings you want validated and we’ll coordinate scheduling (RedSky indicated 2–4 business days of focused work).

Connor will draft the one-page methodology note and the attestation template and drop them into the Drive by tomorrow. Once we have the remediation workbook and either the attestation or retest evidence, you should be in good shape for your 9/15 audit window.
